newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks weaker but off lows.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks weaker but off lows.

text.p: A late buying spree pushed Australian shares off their Wednesday lows to finish just under 20 points down most of the weakness coming from futures selling and a softer Wall Street, brokers said.
The All Ordinaries index ended 19.1 points lower at 2,385.2, but off its low of 2,373.3.
Brokers said selling of the March and June futures contracts pushed the physical market lower, while many investors were nervous about a possible rise in U.S. interest rates.

"The market fell another six points this afternoon on the back of arbitraging, as the SPI (Share Price Index futures contract) was at a 15 point discount (to the physical) and then arbitrageurs came in," said Chris Walker, head of Australian equities at Colonial Investment Management.
Walker said the market was likely to be choppy for the rest of the week as the market took its cue from Wall Street.

"There is still a lot of nervousness surrounding the FOMC (U.S. Federal Open Market Committee) meeting on the 25th next week and you have got triple witching this week in the States. So it tends to be a volatile week and the week after tends to be fairly volatile," Walker said. "A lot of people are sitting on their hands at the moment."

Brokers said there was continued weakness in the shares of media giant News Corp following its planned acquisition of U.S. marketing group Heritage Media Corp due to its issue of new equity and an increase in News Corp's debt profile.
The ordinary shares in Rupert Murdoch's News Corp closed almost four percent lower, making a fall of about nine percent since it announced the Heritage acquisition on Monday.
News Corp preference shares ended 2.7 percent lower for a drop of percent since the announcement.
Major miners were mainly firm despite a fall in base metal prices on Tuesday, with BHP higher and CRA steady.
Oil producer Santos fell about three percent after it made a A$$270 million capital raising to buy oil assets from WMC.
Qantas eased two cents to A$2.45, with the airline announcing just before the market closed that it would sell its stake in Air New Zealand B class shares.

Diversified manufacturer Southcorp topped the turnover list as the stock went ex-dividend. Industrial groups Wesfarmers and Howard Smith were also ex-dividend with both stocks down around three percent.
The media index suffered the largest sector fall, while the telecommunications and engineering sectors were the few to go against the trend.

Brokers said investors were also uncertain about Papua New Guinea-linked stocks due to the political upset earlier this week when the PNG army chief called on Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan to resign over his support for mercenaries on the island of Bougainville.
Anti-government protests today added to the political uncertainty. PNG stocks were mixed with Orogen Minerals and Oil Search both higher, while Lihir Gold and Niugini Mining were both lower.
The March share index futures contract was 23 points lower at 2,365, a 20.5 point discount to the underlying index.
